A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rectified LpJEPA work and contain readable main text and Appendices A–L. The equations, figures, tables, and moved or renumbered material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining, linear-probe, transfer, ablation, and qualitative results, including ImageNet-100 and CIFAR-100 experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds ImageNet-1K evaluation, batch-size sensitivity measurements, and a runtime comparison in Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: The architecture, rectification, RDMReg objective, target sampling, and projection procedures are retained. Eigenvector projections already appeared in v1 Section 4.4 and Figure 14; their ImageNet-1K evaluation does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix J.4 adds pretraining and linear-probe evaluation on full ImageNet-1K, materially expanding class coverage beyond the earlier ImageNet-100 subset. CIFAR-100 and the six transfer datasets are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds a dedicated component-level efficiency comparison against SIGReg in Table 4, absent from v1's reported runtime comparisons. Existing classification and transfer comparator rosters remain unchanged; the new ImageNet-1K experiment reuses VICReg.

E3.justification: New protocols include a controlled 100-epoch ImageNet-1K comparison, a CIFAR-100 batch-size sweep from 24 to 512, and 100-epoch timing measurements with GPU utilization and memory metrics. Settings for the retained experiments are unchanged; the shorter budget is not a revision of the earlier ImageNet-100 runs.

E4.justification: Appendices J.5–J.6 add analyses of batch-size sensitivity and computational overhead. Earlier rectification, scale, projector-dimension, projection-count, eigenvector, transfer-sparsity, and qualitative analyses remain. The additions address practical efficiency without replacing the existing analysis program.

E5.justification: New Table 3 explicitly reports mean ± standard deviation for batch-size experiments, without specifying run counts or seeds. The existing single-run, seed-5 disclosure for ImageNet-100 remains unchanged; an increase in repeated runs for retained results is not established.

E6.justification: Earlier table values are retained, while Tables 2–4 add substantial scalability and efficiency results. On the new 100-epoch ImageNet-1K evaluation, encoder/projector accuracies are 60.52/46.23 for VICReg, 57.95/46.07 for random-projection RDMReg, and 60.63/48.84 with eigenvectors. New findings include batch-size saturation around 128–256 and training times of 19.02 versus 19.27 minutes for SIGReg and RDMReg. These are newly reported experiments, not improvements over matched v1 scores.

T1.justification: Proposition B.9 and its derivation restore the missing Γ(3/p)/Γ(1/p) factor in the second moment. Appendix I distinguishes centered covariance from uncentered second moments and changes the latter's normalization from 1/sqrt(B−1) to 1/sqrt(B). Appendix J.7 adds computational-complexity derivations. The principal entropy and covariance propositions and their proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and first stated contribution narrow the maximum-entropy claim from the rectified distribution itself, up to rescaling, to its continuous truncated component under norm and support constraints. The introduction also removes the associated assertion of preventing collapse even in highly sparse regimes. This materially narrows a central theoretical contribution, while retaining the method and empirical competitiveness claims.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 and Appendix I qualify finite-projection guarantees and replace broad VCReg-recovery interpretations with a conditional covariance connection. Appendix K.2 limits information-retention conclusions to the examined examples. New discussion explains short-training behavior through competing optimization demands and acknowledges computational constraints and unfused kernels. These substantially revise the scope and interpretation of the guarantees.

D1.justification: v2 adds runtime, GPU utilization, and memory measurements, discloses unfused projection/reduction operations, and clarifies ImageNet-100's provenance in Appendix L.1. Existing architecture, optimizer, augmentation, hardware, and code-access information is retained. The new studies do not receive a comparably complete expansion of implementation details.

R1.justification: The cited-work inventory and Appendix A are essentially unchanged. However, Section 4.4 and Appendix I narrow the relationship to VICReg from recovery to a conditional second-order connection and distinguish the NMF-like interpretation from centered covariance regularization.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, theoretical explanations, and qualitative conclusions. Appendix J gains four subsections, terminology and typographical errors are corrected, and an Impact Statement and proceedings notice are added. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables, renumbers the original appendix tables, and relocates Table 1 from page 7 to page 8 alongside Figure 4. Existing figures are retained, with limited caption edits and page reflow rather than substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical accuracy through the moment correction, qualifies overstated guarantees, and adds useful scale, sensitivity, and cost evidence, including an unfavorable ImageNet-1K result. The gains are limited by the restricted 100-epoch comparison, unspecified run counts for the new standard deviations, and incomplete consistency: Section 3.5 still retains the broader maximum-entropy statement narrowed in the abstract.
